summary_en: Mass air flow reading may be outside the expected range. Confirm with live data and intake condition — not a parts order.
Intake air temperature circuit high. Often a connector, open circuit, or sensor issue. Verify with a scan tool.
common_causes: Open circuit in the signal wire

title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
summary_en: Throttle or pedal position signal is out of expected range. Confirm live TP/APP data before assuming a sensor is failed.
common_causes: Throttle body carbon or binding (observe only)
safety_notes: Unexpected throttle response is a stop-driving concern until verified.

title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
summary_en: Throttle or pedal position signal is low. Check connectors and related fuses before replacing parts.
common_causes: Short to ground on the signal wire

title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
summary_en: Throttle or pedal position signal is high. Educational checks start at wiring and live data, not a parts verdict.
common_causes: Short to voltage on the signal wire

title_en: Coolant Thermostat (Coolant Temp Below Thermostat Regulating Temperature)
summary_en: Engine may be slow to reach operating temperature. Thermostat, coolant level, and sensor data should be verified — this is not a command to replace the thermostat today.
common_causes: Thermostat stuck open (confirm with temp rise)

summary_en: Upstream O2/AFR heater circuit. Confirm fuse, connector, and heater operation before assuming the sensor is failed.
Downstream O2 heater circuit. Educational only — verify heater power/ground and live data; do not assume the catalytic converter is failed.
Fuel trim indicates a lean condition on bank 1. Confirm with fuel trims and leak checks — not a single-part verdict.
Lean condition on bank 2. Same educational path as P0171; compare banks before replacing parts.
common_causes: Vacuum or intake leak on bank 2
Exhaust leak near an upstream sensor

summary_en: Misfire detected on multiple cylinders. Educational checks (coils, plugs, intake leaks) are not a repair order.
common_causes: Ignition coil or spark plug wear
safety_notes: If the engine is shaking hard or the MIL is flashing, reduce load and consider a shop. Catalytic converter overheat risk.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 1. Coil/plug swap tests can help; they are educational, not a parts mandate.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: stop aggressive driving and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 2. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Shared intake leak affecting several cylinders
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 3. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 4. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 5. Educational swap tests can help identify coil vs plug vs other causes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 6. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 7. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Misfire isolated to cylinder 8. Same educational caution as other misfire codes.
common_causes: Injector or wiring on that cylinder
Mechanical issue best confirmed at a shop
safety_notes: Flashing MIL: reduce load and verify professionally.

summary_en: Crankshaft position circuit fault. The engine may crank without starting or stall. Confirm connector, air gap, and related fuses — not an automatic sensor replacement.
safety_notes: Stalling in traffic is a safety issue — verify before highway driving.

summary_en: Camshaft position circuit fault. Can cause hard start, rough running, or a no-start. Confirm wiring and correlation data with a scan tool.
EGR flow below expected. Passages, valve, and related sensors need confirmation — do not assume the EGR valve must be replaced from the code alone.
common_causes: EGR valve or solenoid not opening

summary_en: Downstream vs upstream O2 activity suggests catalytic converter efficiency may be low — or sensors/exhaust leaks can mimic it. Do not assert the converter must be replaced.
common_causes: Exhaust leak ahead of the downstream sensor
Catalyst efficiency concern (confirm with live data)

summary_en: Same family as P0420 on bank 2. Educational only; exhaust leaks and O2 sensors can imitate catalyst failure.
common_causes: Catalyst efficiency concern (confirm, do not assume)

summary_en: Small evaporative-emissions leak. Gas cap, hoses, and purge/vent parts are educational starting points — a smoke test confirms.
common_causes: Purge or vent valve sealing issue

summary_en: Large EVAP leak. Loose or missing cap is a common first check. Confirm before replacing canisters or valves.
common_causes: Loose, missing, or damaged gas cap

summary_en: Very small EVAP leak. Often intermittent; a professional smoke test is the reliable confirmation path.
Often associated with a loose fuel cap. Reseat the cap and retest — do not treat this as a failed EVAP canister by default.
Evaporative system flow detected when purge should be closed. Educational checks: purge valve sealing and hose routing — not a canister replacement order.
Vehicle speed signal issue. Can affect ABS or transmission behavior. Verify connectors and related module data.
safety_notes: Verify before driving if the speedometer or ABS warnings are present.

title_en: Idle Control System RPM Higher Than Expected
summary_en: Idle higher than expected. Vacuum leaks and throttle-body cleanliness are educational checks, not a parts order.
common_causes: Throttle body deposit (observe/clean if specified in the manual)

summary_en: Oil pressure sensor/switch circuit fault. Confirm actual oil level and whether a mechanical gauge agrees — do not ignore a low-pressure warning light.
safety_notes: If the oil-pressure warning is on, stop and check level. Continued driving with true low pressure can damage the engine.

summary_en: Oil pressure sensor reading is out of expected range. Compare scan data with oil level and, if possible, a mechanical reading.
safety_notes: Treat a red oil-pressure lamp as urgent until proven otherwise.

summary_en: Oil pressure sensor circuit low. Could be wiring or a true low-pressure condition — verify oil level immediately.
safety_notes: Stop and check oil if a warning lamp is on.

summary_en: Oil pressure sensor circuit high. Confirm wiring and that the reading matches engine behavior; do not ignore conflicting warning lamps.
Charging or battery voltage low. Check battery state and charging output with a meter. Electrical diagnosis first — do not assume an ECU replacement.

title_en: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit / Open
summary_en: Fuel pump control circuit open or not responding as expected. Confirm inertia switch/fuse (if equipped), relay click, and pump power — not an automatic pump replacement.
safety_notes: Fuel work: no sparks, cool system, and follow the owner's manual. A no-start on a live road is a safety issue.

summary_en: PCM request to check TCM/transmission codes. Read transmission-specific codes; P0700 alone is not a rebuild verdict.
common_causes: Stored TCM codes not yet read

title_en: Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
summary_en: Intake cam timing may be more advanced than expected. Confirm oil level/condition and VVT operation with live data — not a command to replace a cam phaser today.
common_causes: Cam phaser or timing chain wear (shop)

title_en: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
summary_en: Downstream oxygen sensor voltage high. Verify connector, wiring, and live data. Do not assume the catalytic converter has failed from this code alone.
common_causes: Exhaust leak near the sensor (confirm, do not replace on guess)

title_en: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
summary_en: Knock sensor circuit. Confirm connector and harness condition. Unexpected spark knock under load is a stop-and-check concern — not an OEM part-number order.
Ignition coil A circuit. Check the coil connector and related misfire codes. Do not invent an OEM coil number from the code alone.
common_causes: Failed coil on cylinder A (confirm swap test if safe)

summary_en: EVAP system fault. Start with the gas cap and visible hoses. This is not a charcoal-canister replacement verdict.
EVAP vent control circuit. Confirm vent valve connector and blocked vent path (aftermarket trays, debris) before parts. Educational checks only.

title_en: Idle Air Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
summary_en: Idle speed lower than expected. Check for vacuum leaks, dirty throttle (observe only), and related idle codes. Not an automatic idle-air-valve replacement.
common_causes: Throttle body carbon (observe; follow manual if cleaning)

summary_en: Internal PCM/ECM processor fault reported. Record freeze frame, check battery/charging voltage, and use a dealer or specialist for module diagnosis — do not replace the PCM from this code alone.

title_en: Throttle Actuator Control System - Stuck Open
summary_en: Electronic throttle may be stuck open. Unexpected acceleration or a throttle warning is a stop-driving concern until verified. Do not 'clean and ignore'.
common_causes: Throttle body carbon or binding (observe only)
safety_notes: If the vehicle surges or will not return to idle, stop driving and use a qualified shop.

title_en: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
summary_en: Upstream O2/AFR signal looks stuck lean. Confirm exhaust leaks, fuel trim, and connector condition — not a single-sensor parts order.
common_causes: Sensor contamination or failure (verify live data)
